children: US tech stocks are entering a pivotal earnings week as investors question whether the AI boom can justify its mounting costs. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.21% on October 23 to close at 25,955.34, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.52% to 7,623.68, extending its weekly decline. With Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon preparing to report results, investors will scrutinize cloud growth, AI monetization, and capital expenditure for signs that heavy investments are translating into sustainable earnings.
The upcoming reports could test whether the recent pullback is a temporary setback or a broader reassessment of AI valuations.
1. Microsoft (MSFT) Stock: Can Azure Growth Ease AI Spending Concerns?

Microsoft reports its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results on October 28, with Wall Street focused on Azure growth, Copilot adoption, and AI infrastructure spending. Analysts expect earnings of $4.71 per share on revenue of $90.63 billion.

The key question is whether accelerating AI demand can support Microsoft’s growth without putting further pressure on margins and cash flow. Investors will also assess management’s outlook for Azure and future capital expenditure.
Strong cloud guidance and evidence of AI monetization could restore confidence. Slower growth or higher-than-expected spending could intensify concerns about investment returns.
2. Alphabet (GOOGL) Stock: Can Google Cloud Strengthen the Earnings Outlook?

Alphabet reports earnings on October 28 as investors assess Google Cloud growth, advertising demand, and the financial impact of AI-powered search. Analysts expect earnings of $3.03 per share on revenue of approximately $127.92 billion.

Google Cloud’s performance will be particularly important as Alphabet expands its AI infrastructure. Meanwhile, investors will look for evidence that AI-powered search can preserve advertising growth while creating new monetization opportunities.

Strong cloud results and resilient advertising revenue could support the stock. Rising investment costs combined with weaker search growth could leave investors questioning the returns from Alphabet’s AI strategy.
3. Amazon (AMZN) Stock: Will AWS Growth Offset Rising AI Costs?

Amazon is scheduled to report earnings on October 29, putting AWS revenue growth, operating margins, and AI infrastructure spending in focus. Analysts expect earnings of $1.96 per share on revenue of approximately $202 billion.

AWS remains central to Amazon’s profitability and AI strategy. Investors will assess whether demand for cloud computing and AI services can sustain growth while the company expands its infrastructure. Retail margins and forward guidance will also influence expectations for overall profitability.
Strong AWS growth and improving margins could support the bullish case. Higher spending without a corresponding improvement in revenue expectations could weigh on investor confidence.
Big Tech Earnings Could Set the Market’s Next Direction

Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon face a common challenge: demonstrating that AI investments can generate sustainable financial returns. Azure, Google Cloud, and AWS growth will offer important clues, but capital expenditure and forward guidance could ultimately determine how investors respond.
If cloud growth and AI monetization exceed expectations, the results could help stabilize US tech stocks. If spending rises faster than returns, the sector’s valuation concerns may persist.

title: US Tech Stocks Under Pressure: 3 Stocks to Watch Before Next Week’s Earnings
